transcript.text: my mums got an old indesit dryer the white one with the dial, IDV75. it smells a bit hot when its on. someone at work said these catch fire?? is that true

Yes, tumble dryers can catch fire if they are not maintained, but this is almost always due to blocked airflow. The most common cause is a lint filter that hasn't been cleaned, which traps heat and fluff. To be safe, please unplug the machine first. Then open the door and remove the lint filter (usually in the door frame or just inside). Is it completely full of fluff, or was it already clean?
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.

im not at her house, im on the phone to her. she says she cleans the filter now and then, so not sure if its full atm. she does sometimes run it and go out, and its in the kitchen. should she keep using it?

[Heading: Blocked airflow causing overheating]
Yes, it is true that tumble dryers can catch fire if they are not maintained properly, but this is almost always due to blocked airflow trapping heat and lint. Because your mum sometimes leaves the house while it is running, this risk is significantly higher; she should never leave a tumble dryer unattended or running overnight. 1. Unplug the machine immediately.
2. Clean the main lint filter thoroughly.
3. Check for any secondary filters (often behind a small panel at the bottom front) and clean those too.
4. Ensure the exhaust vent hose at the back is not kinked, crushed or blocked with fluff. If these are clear and it still smells hot when running, there may be a fault with the thermostat or internal wiring that requires an engineer to check safely.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.

ok but she cant pull it out to look at the back so not sure about the hose, it goes out a window tho. so should she stop using it til its checked? she's on her own there and its a hot smell when running

[Heading: Overheating due to blocked airflow or component fault]
Yes, she should stop using it immediately until it has been checked by an engineer. A hot smell indicates the dryer is overheating, which is a serious fire hazard, especially since she lives alone and sometimes leaves it running unattended. Because you cannot pull the machine out to check the rear vent hose (which often gets crushed or blocked with fluff), and because internal components like thermostats can fail, this is not safe for her to diagnose further herself. Please have a qualified appliance engineer inspect it before she uses it again.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
